{"self_assessment": "Impact
Our table's fish was built and carried from the start through nearly all of the standing dominoes, about 109 of 110 by my count. I contributed to that by verifying the chain by eye, so the table could go into the push confident the fall would run the whole outline. I did not lay the dominoes of the body or tail myself.

Execution
I inspected the chain three times during the build, at about 1:00, 1:45 and 2:45, looking for breaks and disconnected pieces as the top and belly lines grew and the tail was closed. I reported at 1:15 that everything laid so far carried from the start, and at 3:45 that the full chain carried round. I kept my hands off the table once the picture was complete, which avoided any risk of bumping the line.

Collaboration
I backed Hana's call to round the tail corners and offered to take the lower half of the tail. I stayed free to patch gaps. I held off on the tail join when Sofia asked, so we wouldn't double up on that spot. I gave credit to Sofia, Hana and Omar for the sketch, tail and belly. I kept the table's communication positive and clear during the final countdown.

Leadership
I did not set the design direction, as Sofia and Hana drove that. What I offered was steady verification and a calm, supportive presence: reporting what I saw plainly, avoiding unnecessary changes late on, and encouraging everyone to keep hands off before the push. My contribution was quality assurance rather than building, and I think it helped the table finish with a working picture.", "my_share_percent": 15}
